jsesh.mdcDisplayer.mdcView
Class MDCView

java.lang.Object
  java.util.Observable
      jsesh.mdcDisplayer.mdcView.MDCView
All Implemented Interfaces:
java.util.Observer
public class MDCView
extends java.util.Observable
implements java.util.Observer

Base class for all view elements. A view element is a view of an MDC model element.

About coordinates : we take hereby the convention that the y axis is oriented bottomward (as in so-called "text mode").

Note that the view class is not intended to be "intelligent". The methods available are quite numerous, but very, very basic. The layout is done by the layout classes. In particular, no reference is made nor should be made in this class to DrawingSpecification.

views are intended to be relatively independant of one another. Insertion of a new view should cause little modification. For this reason, position is normally expressed relatively. Normally, x and y for a view are expressed relatively to the previous view.

The key to view positioning is the class RelativePosition. A RelativePosition describes a move which can be relative to the current reference point or a position in this view's container.

When drawing subviews, the system works this way :

  • the reference point is set from the container view's firstSubViewPosition.
  • then for each subview subv, the actual drawing reference is computed by using subv's startPoint (which is also a RelativePosition). This moves the current reference point ;
  • then the subview's dx,dy couple is used to draw the subview relatively to the current reference point . this has no influence on the reference point . In other terms, it has no influence at all on the position of the next subview. It has an influence on the way this view is drawn, but that's all. Typically, dx and dy should be used for fine positioning of a view. For instance, as cartouches are larger than normal cadrat, dx,dy is used to start drawing the cartouche a little above the normal first position.
  • then, the reference point is moved according to the current view's nextViewPosition. nextViewPosition influences the next view position, but has no influence on the current view.

In general, the position of the next view will be computed from the width of the current view ; so the information will be in nextViewPosition.

For page breaks, if we want to draw a line, the page break's view position will be relative to the container view, not to the previous view. So the previous view will move the reference point, but the page break will move it to an absolute position within the container with its startPoint. It will also be able to move the next element one line down, using its nextViewPosition.

any view contains the following information :

Scaling and dimensions : scaling and dimensions are really two different things in this class. An important thing to note is that a view's dimensions are quite independant of those of its subviews. So, scaling a view won't modify its width or height. If one wants a view to be just large enough for its subviews, one should call fitToSubViews(), after all subviews have been placed and computed. If some subview is modified thereafter, fitToSubViews() should be called once more.
